Many reviews have emerged on their
preparation and transformation.<sup>2</sup> Among them, the transi-
tion-metal-catalyzed asymmetric hydrofunctionalization of
allenes represents an important domain in allene chemistry.
It is a powerful means to construct allyl C−C and C−X bonds
with chiral carbon centers from allenes, and it can also directly
give rise to many natural and non-natural products as well as
some important pharmaceutical molecules.<sup>3</sup> In these reactions,
Rh and Ir catalysts are commonly used to achieve the
formation of chiral branched products, but most need a higher
temperature or longer reaction time.<sup>4</sup> As a comparison, Pd-
catalyzed asymmetric functionalization reactions of allenes
have been extremely scarce until now.<sup>5</sup> In addition, Pd-
catalyzed hydrofunctionalization of allenes usually results in a
dominated linear allyl product (Scheme 1a).<sup>6</sup> And compared
with the alkylallenes, the arylallenes are relatively dificult
substrates and more inclined to render the linear products
without branched products, as may be due to electronic efects
and conjugated efects as well as possible steric efects of the
aromatic ring on the arylallenes.<sup>7</sup> Therefore, it is highly
desirable to regulate the branched regioselectivity of the
asymmetric hydrofunctionalization of allenes precisely and
remains greatly challenging, especially for the arylallenes.
Considering that, we herein focus on the asymmetric
hydrosulfonylation of simple terminal allenes including alkyl-
and arylallenes, with the aim of the synthesis of diverse chiral
allylsulfones, which are the ubiquitous building blocks of the
drugs and natural products (Scheme 1b).<sup>8</sup> Breit and his co-
workers developed a Rh-catalyzed asymmetric hydrothioeth-
eration oxidation of allenes in a two-step process to aford the
chiral allylsulfones. In their reaction, excessive oxidants and
smelly sulfur-containing toxic reagents were used and only
limited to alkylallenes (Scheme 1c, Breit’s work).<sup>9</sup> Recently,
Aponick and co-workers reported an asymmetric hydro-
sulfonylation reaction of allenes through using a Rh catalyst
(Scheme 1c, Aponick’s work).<sup>10</sup> In their work, the arylallenes
delivered the corresponding allyl sulfones with relatively low
enantioselectivities. In spite of this, we herein developed a Pd-
catalyzed/ligand-controlled asymmetric hydrosulfonylation of

K _ { \mathrm { H } } / K _ { \mathrm { D } }
ratio of 1.8 demonstrated that this
reaction was not first-order KIE and that the cleavage of the
O−H bond was not the rate-determining step. And the 61%
deuterated product 3aa-d indicated that the hydrogen at the

trace of water in the reaction system, solvent, or reactants
(Scheme S1b). Combining these results with the absolute
configuration of 3oa and 3sa determined by the single X-ray
difraction (see Figures S1 and S2), we proposed a possible
transition-state model (Figure S3). In the system of (S, Rp)-
Josiphos with allyl palladium, the sulfinic acid prefers the Si
face instead of the Re face to attack and gives the 3oa. In the

Scheme 2. Plausible catalytic cycle for the arylallenes
inserts into the O−H bond of RSO H to generate an M−H
intermediate (INT-A). Subsequently, the allene compound
undergoes a hydrogenation reaction, resulting in the formation
of a π-allyl palladium complex (INT-B). Following this step,
the lone pair of electrons on the sulfur atom attacks the π-allyl
group while simultaneously cleaving the Pd−O bond to form a

palladium, resulting in the formation of the final product and

To further understand how the catalyst controls regiose-
lectivity and stereoselectivity, we selected the Pd/L18-
catalyzed reaction of arylallenes as a model for density
functional theory (DFT) calculations, focusing on locating
the transition state structure of this conversion process. We
located the transition states corresponding to the generation of
linear and branched products (R, S), and we calculated their
relative energies. As shown in Figure S4 (for more less-
favorable transition states, see the Supporting Information file),
the transition state (TS-branched-S) for generating the S-
branched product possesses the lowest energy, while the
energy of its enantiomer product (TS-branched-R) is 2.6 kcal/
mol higher. The computational results predict that the ee value
of the branched product is approximately 95% at 323 K, which
aligns closely with experimental observations. Concurrently,
our calculations show that the relative energy of the transition
state leading to linear product formation (TS-Linear) is
comparable to that of TS-branched-S (ΔΔG = 1.0 kcal/mol),
which is consistent with experimental findings and further
consolidates that b/l regioselective control is very dificult.
Further analysis of relevant transition state structures reveals
that in TS-Linear, during S−C bond formation, there has been
a significant transformation from an
\eta ^ { 3 } \mathrm { - P d }
structure to an π-Pd
structure. The conjugation between the carbon−carbon double
bond in the linear product and its aromatic group contributes
to enhance electronic stability, explaining why arylallene
typically favors linear product generation as noted in previous
studies. Although steric hindrance exists between phosphorus
ligands on the catalyst and two aromatic groups along with
their functional groups within TS-Linear, rendering it less
favorable compared to TS-branched-S, a comprehensive
consideration of both electronic efects and steric hindrance
indicates that their final energy diference remains relatively
small. In addition, we are pleased to report that 1,1-substituted
allene substrates can also produce highly enantioenriched
branched products with the Pd-L18 chiral metal complex,
thereby providing an efective approach for constructing chiral
quaternary carbon centers. The corresponding transition state
structures are also calculated, and the computational results
show that the relative energy diference between TS-branched
S-Me and TS-branched-R-Me has not decreased (more details
shown in SI), thus maintaining a high stereochemical
selectivity.

reaction of allenes; only one chiral allylsulfone with a
quaternary carbon stereocenter was obtained in low
enantioselectivity. In addition to the experimental results on
